questions.q: Why is it inaccurate to describe the audit/SIEM discrepancy as an unplanned detour from this capstone's real work?
options: Because the discrepancy was scripted into the course from the very beginning for dramatic effect
Because catching exactly this kind of gap was the whole reason the dual-check automation checked group membership, direct grants, and SIEM telemetry independently instead of trusting one method
Because the discrepancy didn't involve any real data
Because the OT/SCADA segment was rebuilt from scratch afterward
questions.explain: The dual-check design existed specifically so two independent methods could disagree and surface a real gap — which is exactly what happened, proving the architecture's value rather than interrupting it.

questions.q: What did the Beginner tier of this capstone sequence build, for which stakeholder?
options: A dual-cloud identity consolidation, for CISO Howard Okonjo
A baseline security hardening pass across Windows and Linux servers and Mara Voss's first working Sentinel detection rule, for IT Manager Dale Granger
A zero-trust pilot on the OT/SCADA segment
A board-level security report
questions.explain: The Beginner tier was the narrowest of the three: a hardening pass and one Sentinel rule, for a single stakeholder, Dale Granger.

questions.q: Which real-world progression does this lesson say a security engineer's career path commonly follows, building on work like this capstone?
options: There is no realistic next step beyond this capstone
Toward security architect or GRC leadership work — deeper architecture review, formal program ownership, and credentials like Security+, CySA+, and CISSP along the way
Immediately into an unrelated field with no connection to security
Back to an entry-level help-desk role
questions.explain: This lesson grounds the next step in the catalog's own Zero Trust and GRC courses' progression — toward architecture or GRC leadership, with relevant credentials, not in a certificate alone.

questions.q: Which of the following is named as a real, deliberately out-of-scope extension a genuinely senior version of this program would still push further on?
options: Automated cross-tool reconciliation run continuously, instead of catching gaps only when an audit happens to run close enough to the automation to compare
Removing the GRC risk register entirely since the finding is already closed
Eliminating break-glass access everywhere with no exceptions ever
Combining the OT/SCADA segment back into the flat network
questions.explain: Continuous automated reconciliation, extending the fixed methodology to every segment, and a formal org-wide break-glass expiry policy are all named as honest, deliberate scope boundaries — not oversights.

questions.q: What is the single most important thing this capstone sequence demonstrated, according to this final lesson?
options: That Sentinel is a better tool than any competing SIEM in all cases

That building independent checks on purpose, so they can disagree, gives a real organization a genuine chance of catching a gap before it reaches a board meeting — which it did, for real, in this capstone
That compliance audits are unnecessary once automation exists
That zero trust eliminates the need for any further stakeholder negotiation
questions.explain: The capstone's throughline, across all three tiers, is that deliberately independent validation methods catching a real disagreement is the architecture succeeding, not failing.
